note: Both sets cover essentially the same member schedule facts (W8X10, W10X12, W6X20, HSS4X4X1/4, HSS4X6X1/4, PL3X1/4, L3x3x1/4, L4X4X5/16, C8X11.5, C3X6) plus the T.O. STEEL 11'-4" and SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0" datums, and both carry the same three misbound elevation conditions (L4X4X5/16 tagged to West though it appears in the East and South elevations, C8X11.5 tagged to East though it is in the West elevation, and C3X6 tagged to West though it is in the North/Bedroom elevation and is a channel, not a beam). Set A and Set B also share the same vague entities ("member", "component", "framing member") and the same duplicate restatements of L3x3x1/4", W6X20, W10X12, PL3X1/4 and C8X11.5 under two names. Set B adds one extra redundant L3x3x1/4" claim with the sheet title as its condition, while Set A adds redundant W6X20/W8X10/C8X11.5 restatements, so the net engineering content and error count are equivalent.
remarks: Both sets omit the elevation dimensions that carry real engineering information on this sheet: 32'-0" and 27'-8" building lengths, 12'-0"/10'-0"/3'-1" and 7'-6"/5'-6"/2'-0"/9'-0" bay and offset dimensions, FIRST FLR at 2'-4" and GRADE LEVEL at 0", the 8'-8 5/8" / 8'-8 1/2" and 8" clearances, and the 1/4" = 1'-0" scale. Neither set binds any section size to a specific gridline or member mark, so all section claims are effectively unlocated lists of shapes. The text layer is a flat dump with no spatial grouping, so elevation attribution had to be reconstructed from gridline sets and reference callouts (A1/C4 vs C1/A4, S-701 refs) and cross-checked against the image; label-level verification in the image is limited by resolution.
